newsitem.title: USA: Arco, Lukoil to sign $5.2 billion joint venture.
newsitem.headline: Arco, Lukoil to sign $5.2 billion joint venture.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield Co., seeking to boost its overseas oil reserves, said Friday it planned to sign a $5.2 billion joint venture pact with Russian oil giant Lukoil.
Arco President Mike Bowlin and Lukoil President Vagit Alekperov were scheduled to finalize the 18-year agreement, announced last September, at a signing ceremony at the Russian Embassy in Washington.

"This is a big day for Arco," Bowlin said in Washington at a luncheon for the Moscow International Petroleum Club, adding the long-term agreement was "one that will be beneficial to both companies and to both countries."
Although the agreement was reached last September, Arco officials said the terms were only finalized in the last few days.

Initial projects include a 12.5 percent stake in the Caspian Pipeline Consortium (CPC), a line expected to carry oil from Kazakstan to Russia's Black Sea, and a 5 percent ownership in the Tengiz oil field in Kazakstan.
Industry analysts said Arco, which owns 8 percent of Lukoil, is signing the agreement in order to establish a long-term framework to develop oil and gas projects in the former Soviet Union.

"I think this is a company that needs foreign reserves. They have cash and they need to grow or they won't survive," said Holly Gustafson, vice president and senior analyst for NatWest Securities Corp.
Despite growth in worldwide reserves, Los Angeles-based Arco's yearly production from Prudhoe Bay, once its premier oil field in Alaska, has declined about 12 percent
Kenneth Dickerson, a senior vice president of Arco, said Arco wanted to team up with a Russian company before investing heavily in Russia and other former Soviet Republics.
"This gives us a better chance to extend the relationship long-term," he said.

Until now, Arco has failed to establish a strong overseas presence, according to oil industry analysts. But Friday's deal with cash-strapped Lukoil gives the U.S. oil giant a powerful political ally in the former Soviet Union.
Lukoil has been trying to expand its operations in the former Soviet Union by signing deals with western oil firms.
Lukoil is currently in talks with Chevron Corp. to acquire a 5 percent stake from Chevron in the $20 billion Tengiz oil project in Kazakhstan.
